title: Incident writeup (Drive): Scheduler capacity incident caused elevated queueing and timeouts
body:
Summary
Customer-impacting incident on 2026-04-02 where hosted API requests experienced elevated queue time and timeouts due to scheduler capacity shortfall in us-east. This is the canonical writeup; it was not ported to Confluence because SRE used the Drive template this quarter.

Customer impact
- Yes. Elevated timeouts and latency for hosted API (chat + embeddings).
- Duration: 54 minutes (from first SLO burn to recovery).

Owning engineering team
- Site Reliability Engineering (Capacity & Fleet)

What happened (high-level)
- A GPU fleet maintenance window reduced available schedulable capacity.
- Autoscaler policy did not react due to a misconfigured safety cap introduced earlier in the week.
- Queue depth grew, pushing time_to_first_token and overall latency beyond SLOs; some clients hit timeout limits.

Timeline (UTC)
- 14:03 Alerts: p95 queue_time and SLO burn rate in us-east
- 14:08 On-call confirms capacity deficit (available_gpus < expected)
- 14:17 Found autoscaler cap set to 0 for one pool
- 14:22 Hotfixed autoscaler policy + manually added 32 GPUs from warm pool
- 14:41 Queue depth begins draining
- 14:57 Back within SLO

Root cause
Misconfigured autoscaler safety cap for pool us-east-a100-80gb prevented scale-out during a planned maintenance window. The maintenance reduced capacity, but the scale controller interpreted the cap as an intentional limit and refused to add nodes.

Follow-ups
- Add config linting to prevent cap=0 in production pools (Owner: SRE; Due: 2026-04-20)
- Require pre-maintenance capacity simulation for high-traffic pools (Owner: SRE; Due: 2026-04-30)
- Add alert on discrepancy between planned maintenance capacity and effective schedulable capacity (Owner: SRE; Due: 2026-05-05)
